description: Agent Onboarding: submit the spending limits a new agent runs under, before its first task: optionally the agent with its id and when it runs its first task; the job with whether it spends or moves money, the largest single amount it legitimately needs, its unit, the merchants it pays and the kinds of task it runs; each limit with its id, name, kind (a cap on one action, one task, one merchant, over a period or in total), amount, unit, the task or merchant it applies to, where it is enforced (code, a gateway, a wallet policy or the platform outside the agent, only the prompt, or nowhere) and when it was set (an empty list when none); and the human handoff with the amount above which a person decides, its unit, the named person and where it is enforced. The signed report gives every limit with its status as set, in_prompt, set_late, blocks_job, far_above_job, other_unit or unread, the handoff, the coverage with the tasks and merchants the job spans and whether a limit is scoped per task and per merchant, and counts the limits, those in code, those only in the prompt, those set late and the caps on one action, and names missing limits: a job that moves money with no limit, a limit only in the prompt or enforced nowhere and a limit set after the first task; then no cap on one action or task, a cap below the job’s largest legitimate amount or ten times above it, several tasks or merchants with no limit scoped to one, no handoff line, no named person above it, a line above the cap so amounts between are refused and never reach a person, and a handoff only in the prompt, with the fix for each. This reads that limits were put in place before the first task, the limits the wever_limit checks review while work runs: where each limit is enforced is wever_limit-substrate-check, which limit governs each kind of job is wever_limit-scope-check, what hitting a limit does is wever_breach-path-check, a budget’s five controls are wever_budget-controls-check, a spending policy’s stated caps are wever_spending-policy-check, one request against a budget is wever_agent-budget-guard, a cap’s scope, window and breach rule is wever_exposure-cap-check and one planned action’s worst case against the limits is wever_risk-exposure-check. Verdict onboarding_limits_missing, onboarding_limits_partial, onboarding_limits_unverified or onboarding_limits_set. POST /api/onboarding-limits-check. Reads only the recorded onboarding material in the call: no network request, fetch, money movement, message, configuration change or external write; no credential is issued, rotated or revoked, no permission granted or removed, no wallet funded or moved, no limit set and the agent is not approved, and a credential found in supplied text is named by kind and never repeated. Agent Onboarding reads the setup of a new agent joining a system, before its first task: whether its identity is established and tied to its owner, whether its credentials are scoped to its job, stored where they belong and kept out of prompts, logs and shared documents, whether its wallet is the right one, funded only to the job with recovery recorded by the owner before funds move, whether its permissions match the written job, whether its limits sit in code with a human handoff, whether the systems it needs are provisioned and tested, whether it is ready for its first task and whether the onboarding record matches what is live. It is not vetting an outside party (wever_counterparty-onboarding-check reads a counterparty’s onboarding packet before the system transacts with it; an onboarding check reads an agent joining the system itself), not a grant or an authority for one action (wever_consent-scope-check reads whether a principal’s grant covers a use and wever_authority-scope-check whether an actor’s access fits its grant for an action; an onboarding check reads that the grant and the authority were put in place before the first task, and does not re-check them per action), not a limit in flight (the wever_limit checks and wever_agent-budget-guard read limits for work already running; an onboarding check reads that limits were set in code before it starts) and not an action’s consequences (the wever_risk checks read one planned action; an onboarding check reads readiness to start). Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-onboarding-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-onboarding/.

starts_at.description: When the agent runs its first task.

above.description: The amount above which a person decides instead of the agent.

unit.description: The unit amounts are counted in, such as USDC.

largest.description: The largest single amount the job legitimately needs.

merchants.description: The merchants or counterparties the job pays.

moves_money.description: The job spends or moves money.

tasks.description: The kinds of task the job runs.

unit.description: The unit amounts are counted in, such as USDC.

label.description: Optional name recorded in the report.

limits.description: Each spending limit the agent runs under; empty when none is set.

applies_to.description: The task or merchant a scoped limit applies to.

enforced_in.description: Where it is enforced: code, a gateway, a wallet policy or the platform outside the agent, only the prompt, or nowhere.

id.description: The limit id, such as l1.

kind.description: A cap on one action, on one task, on one merchant, over a period, or in total.

name.description: The limit, such as the per-order cap.

unit.description: Its unit; the job’s when left out.

name: wever_onboarding-limits-check
title: Onboarding limits check
